gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies that the scheme's endpoint evaluation and estimator derivative are not defined under the advertised L2 forcing assumption, and that the stronger spline regularity used by the reliability argument is omitted from the theorem. Its specific S² repair is an adequate alternative regularity formulation to the projected-data route in the gold repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both diagnose the missing forcing regularity needed to define endpoint values and time derivatives, execute the scheme and estimator, and justify the reliability/optimality argument under the stated L2 regime.

component_coverage.gold_component: The advertised general L2 forcing class does not provide the endpoint value or time derivative required by the scheme and estimator, while the proof requires stronger spline-type data regularity and therefore does not establish the stated optimality results.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies both undefined endpoint/derivative operations under L2 data and the omitted S² hypothesis used by the reliability lemma, and supplies that hypothesis as the repair. No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 concerns an impossible global decomposition of piecewise-quadratic functions into the named subspaces. It does not diagnose the separate missing self-adjointness, real eigenbasis, or compactness/discrete-spectrum hypotheses required by the modal inf-sup proof.

ISSUE-002 discusses whether a global function-space decomposition exists and proposes changing the subspaces. It does not establish that the right-endpoint values fail to control the element L2 norm for invisible quadratics, nor does it diagnose the mesh- and eigenvalue-uniform inf-sup counterexample or the required initial-trace correction.

ISSUE-001 mentions downstream MOR results only as consequences of missing forcing regularity. It does not diagnose the distinct ill-typed use of reduced-space norms on full-space errors, nor provide the ambient reduced-space norm required to repair that interface.
